title: Granular econ + latency diagnostics — prototype notes
summary: Working notes for a diagnostic dashboard that surfaces per-token cost and per-token latency breakdowns. Focus is on quick investigator flows: find expensive tokens, correlate to model variant and batching, and create a lightweight comparison mode (baseline vs rollout). This doc consolidates UX ideas, prototype states, data contract questions, and a prioritized backlog for initial MVP and next two iterations.
body:
Overview:

Problem: engineering and platform teams need to quickly understand cost and latency drivers at token granularity when debugging regressions or tuning inference settings (batching, kv-cache hit rates, quantization). Current console views show aggregated per-request cost and average latency by model; we need an investigative layer that answers: which tokens, prompts, or request patterns are driving unit costs and tail latency?

Primary goals:
- Surface tokens / prefixes with outsized cost or latency contribution.
- Show attribution across the stack: tokenizer -> model variant -> batch size -> hardware pool -> routing fallback.
- Fast pivoting: filter by time window, customer, route, model version, rollout cohort.
- Lightweight compare mode: baseline vs candidate rollout to show delta on token and invocation metrics.
- Instrumentation-ready: UI interactions map back to concrete telemetry queries (Jira refs) so SREs and infra can add indexes/rollups.

Personas and use cases:
- Platform engineer: chase a sudden spike in per-token billable tokens after a new model rollout. Needs to know if tokenizer change or different EOS handling caused extra tokens.
- ML engineer: verify that quantization/EMA/kv-cache changes reduce per-token costs and don't increase 99th-percentile latency.
- Customer success / Solutions engineer: explain to a tiered customer why their cost changed; generate a short report with 3 most influential tokens and recommended tunables.

Key metrics to display (not exhaustive):
- tokens_per_invocation (median / p95 / p99)
- token_cost_contribution (currency units per token aggregated across selection)
- token_latency_contribution (ms per token with breakdown by compute vs io vs queuing)
- batch_effect (delta when same token served in different batch sizes)

Prototype states (three quick screens):
1) Overview lane (investigator landing):
   - Top summary bar: selected filters, top change drivers, quick action buttons (open query, copy permalink, report).
   - Sparkline grid: per-model and per-route token-cost trend small multiples.
   - "Top offending tokens" panel: horizontally scrollable list with token string, avg cost delta, p95 latency delta, sample rate. Clicking token opens token detail.

2) Token detail pane (split right):
   - Waterfall by phase: tokenizer time, model token inference time, kv-cache hit/miss indicator, batch queuing time. Each bar stacked and normalized per-invocation.
   - Table of sampled invocations: timestamp, route, model, batch_size, token_index, token_text_preview(hashes), total_cost_for_invocation, latency_ms. Link to raw request (authed).
   - Small chart: distribution of preceding prefix lengths (to detect long context causing cost spikes).

3) Compare mode overlay:
   - Two columns: baseline / candidate. Each column shows same token waterfall and table; delta column highlights % change and flags like "kv-cache drop" or "model switch".
   - Toggle to show aggregated cohort (all tokens matching prefix / regex).

Controls and filters: time window (presets + exact), route dropdown, model + variant + quantization filter, region, customer id, rollout cohort tag, min-invocation-count slider, token regex. Also sampling control for large selections.

Data contract questions for infra/observability (for dev ticketing):
- telemetry event schema: ensure token_index and token_text (or token_hash) included on request-log events. (JIRA: OBS-2019)
- include batch_size, queue_time_ms, model_variant, device_type, kv_cache_hit boolean per request. (JIRA: OBS-2021)
- derive per-token compute_ms from model-side traces (approx at token-level) or annotate using per-step deltas in the serving runtime (OBS-2035).
- retention: keep raw per-token logs for 7 days; keep preagg summaries for 90 days. (cost/GDPR tradeoffs)

Implementation notes / perf constraints:
- For the landing/top lists, use precomputed token-aggregation tables keyed by (token_hash, model_variant, route, day/hour).
- For token detail on a narrow selection, run sampled raw-query with limit 500 and background async expand if user asks for more.
- Use server-side streaming to send initial summary and then populate sampled invocation table.
- Watchcard: cardinality explosion (many unique tokens). Mitigate with top-K, token clustering (subword groups), and regex grouping.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Investigator landing shows top-20 tokens for a given route/model/window with cost and latency deltas, UI latency < 1s for default filters.
- Token detail panel renders waterfall and 50-sample invocation table; links to request logs for authenticated users.
- Compare mode shows aligned baseline/candidate delta for single token.
- Instrumentation tasks created in OBS backlog and data contracts signed off by infra.

Backlog (prioritized):
- [P0] MVP frontend: landing + token detail + compare mode (est. 8pt dev, 3pt design).
- [P0] Telemetry: add token_index and token_hash to request logs (OBS-2019) (est. 5pt infra).
- [P1] Pre-agg pipeline: hourly token aggregates per model/route (est. 13pt infra).
- [P1] Sampling UX: sample-size control and explanation tooltip (est. 3pt design/dev).
- [P2] Regex / cohort grouping: allow grouping tokens by regex and show group-level contribution (est. 8pt).
- [P2] Automated anomaly flagging: simple threshold-based detector for sudden token cost spikes (est. 5pt infra + 3pt frontend).
- [P3] Customer report export: PDF summary with top 3 tokens and suggested actions (est. 5pt).

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Should token_text ever be stored in a searchable index? Risky for privacy; alternative: reversible per-customer token mapping behind enterprise-only feature.
- Sampling policy: deterministic sampling by hash vs time-slice sampling — deterministic helps reproducibility but can bias.
- How to surface tokenizer-configuration differences across model versions (vocab merges, BPE changes) in a way that is actionable?

Next steps / immediate action items:
- Sync with OBS team to validate event schema and retention (owners: Omar + Ruth). Due EOD next Wed.
- Design touchpoint: produce 3 low-fi screens showing landing + token detail + compare annotations (owner: Ellen). Initial mocks by 2026-03-08.
- Create infra tickets for pre-agg and telemetry fields (owner: Marco).

Notes to reviewer:
- This is intentionally investigative-first; keep scope tight for MVP. The main value is in enabling fast root-cause for cost regressions and giving ML teams a reproducible way to compare changes.
- Feedback wanted on: default sampling strategy, sensible retention windows for summaries, and what rollout metadata fields are critical for alignment.

Edge-case examples (to test in acceptance):
- Very long context windows where tokens near EOS disproportionately increase cost due to kv-cache miss pattern.
- Short repeated tokens (e.g., repeated punctuation or templated outputs) inflating per-token counts but not necessarily expensive; need to show normalized contribution.
- Multilingual token handling where tokenization differences lead to many rare tokens appearing.

References and inspiration:
- internal: per-invocation-cost-explorer (legacy) doc link: CONFLUENCE-UI-666
- external: "Span-level cost attribution" paper notes (link in confluence)
backlog: P0: MVP frontend landing + detail + compare (8pt)
P2: Regex grouping and cohort aggregation (8pt)
P2: Anomaly detector for token spikes (8pt)
unresolved_questions: Should token_text be indexed/searchable or only token_hash stored?
Deterministic vs time-based sampling: which to adopt for reproducibility?
Retention window for raw per-token logs vs pre-aggregates (cost vs compliance)?
